stories.title: IBCC plans fully online attestation from Jan 1, ending office visits and courier submissions
summary: The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) will launch a fully online attestation service on Jan 1, 2027, allowing students to apply for attestation and download their attested documents without visiting an IBCC office or sending documents by courier.

Dr Mallah said the commission had developed the system on the directions of Federal Secretary for Education and Professional Training Nadeem Mahbub, after the IBCC Board of Governors took up the automation of the entire attestation process.
He said the commission expected the service to benefit an estimated 400,000 to 500,000 students by cutting travel and courier costs and saving them time spent visiting and waiting at IBCC offices.

Maaz Sadaqat plays a shot during the Asia Cup Rising Stars match against India A on Nov 22. — Photo courtesy ACC Maaz, registering his second consecutive half-century, made 59 off 63 balls, with six fours and a six, before being caught off Suryansh Shedge in the 20th over.

stories.title: Oman to supply petroleum products, $200m credit facility to PSO under new agreement
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Oman on Sunday signed an agreement under which the Gulf country’s state-owned OQ Trading would supply petroleum products, as well as a $200 million credit line, to the Pakistan State Oil (PSO).
Following the meeting, the two ministers witnessed the signing of a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for petroleum products between PSO and OQ Trading (OQT), Oman’s global commodity trading company.

According to the Petroleum Division, OQT’s LPG supplies to Pakistan are expected to exceed 120,000 metric tonnes by the end of 2026, reflecting the company’s continued commitment to meeting market demand and maintaining energy flows amid regional supply disruptions.
